reference.source: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology / Von Noorden's Binocular Vision and Ocular Motility
clinicalPearls: Presents with near-work asthenopia: eyestrain, headache, blurred or intermittent double vision, and loss of place when reading
The hallmark signs are a receded near point of convergence and reduced fusional (positive) convergence amplitudes at near
An exophoria that is greater at near than at distance is characteristic
Symptoms worsen with prolonged reading or screen use and toward the end of the day
It is a common, usually benign binocular disorder, particularly in students and those doing sustained near work
Orthoptic vision therapy, including convergence exercises such as pencil push-ups and computer-based programmes, is the mainstay of treatment
Base-in prisms or added near correction may relieve symptoms when exercises alone are insufficient
New or atypical convergence insufficiency in an adult should prompt exclusion of a neurological cause
reference.pathophysiology: Convergence insufficiency is a disorder of the near-response fusional vergence system in which the eyes cannot sustain the inward turning needed for comfortable single binocular vision at near. Fusional convergence reserves are inadequate to control an exophoric tendency that is greatest at near fixation, so maintaining alignment during reading demands excessive effort, producing asthenopic symptoms and intermittent diplopia. It is usually idiopathic, but reduced convergence can also follow head injury or accompany neurological disorders that affect the midbrain vergence centres.
additionalDifferentials: Accommodative insufficiency or other accommodative dysfunction
Convergence paralysis from a dorsal midbrain (pretectal) lesion
Parkinsonism and other neurodegenerative disorders affecting vergence
Post-concussion or traumatic brain injury vision syndrome
Myasthenia gravis with variable, fatigable diplopia
additionalInvestigations: Measurement of the near point of convergence
Cover testing at distance and near to demonstrate near exophoria
Assessment of positive fusional vergence amplitudes at near
Cycloplegic refraction and assessment of accommodative function
Best-corrected visual acuity and full orthoptic evaluation
Neurological assessment and imaging if an organic or acquired cause is suspected
redFlags: Sudden-onset convergence problems with other neurological signs suggesting dorsal midbrain syndrome
Associated pupillary or eyelid abnormalities, or a gaze palsy
Convergence failure following significant head trauma with persistent symptoms
Progressive or fatigable diplopia suggesting a neuromuscular disorder
reference.prognosis: Convergence insufficiency generally responds well to vision therapy, with many patients achieving durable relief of symptoms; recurrence can occur and may require refresher exercises, while cases secondary to neurological disease follow the course of the underlying condition.
pitfalls: Attributing reading difficulty to a learning or attentional problem without checking the near point of convergence
Overlooking uncorrected refractive error or accommodative dysfunction
Missing a neurological cause of acquired convergence failure in adults
Prescribing reading glasses that relieve accommodation but worsen the exophoria
references: Von Noorden's Binocular Vision and Ocular Motility
management: Orthoptic vision therapy is the mainstay: supervised office-based vergence and accommodative training to improve fusional convergence
Prescribe home-based convergence exercises such as pencil push-ups and computer-based vergence programmes
Correct any underlying refractive error and treat coexisting accommodative dysfunction
Consider base-in prism spectacles for symptomatic relief in patients who cannot tolerate or complete vision therapy
Advise near-work ergonomics, regular breaks and reduced sustained screen time to limit asthenopic symptoms
Arrange orthoptic follow-up with refresher exercises given the tendency to recur
Refer for neurological assessment and neuroimaging when an acquired cause such as head injury or midbrain pathology is suspected
